11.description: Saskatoon's planning and development process, guided by the Official Community Plan, was presented, detailing how growth and land use decisions are made.

12.description: Saskatoon approved a discretionary use application for a commercial multi-sports and cross-training school at 119 105th Street East, allowing up to 30 students and 5 staff.

chips.text: Residents within 150 meters of 119 105th Street East were notified.

15.description: Approves rezoning 1224 College Drive from M2 to CS1, allowing for mixed-use development consistent with the College Quarter plan. This consolidates it with adjacent CS1 properties.

chips.text: Werkliv Developments applied for the rezoning.

13.description: City Council approved redesignating 133 108th Street West from low-density to medium-density residential and rezoning it from R2 to RM3 District, allowing for higher density development.

chips.text: Commission debated evaluating the application based on full RM3 potential
Residents of Sutherland neighbourhood expressed concerns about increased traffic, parking
Administration recommended denial, citing non-alignment with infill policies and local area plan.
Public engagement raised concerns that approving this application would create a precedent.
Councillor Derek noted the 1999 local area plan encouraged six-unit townhouse developments.

16.description: Saskatoon updated its sign regulations to clarify rules for digital and project development signs, aiming to reduce appeals and address complaints about lighting and separation distances.

chips.text: Digital billboards were incorporated into the bylaw when technology first emerged.
Residential areas and natural areas will see digital signs de-energized at night.
Regulations reference the city's green infrastructure strategy map 18.

9.description: Saskatoon approved a daycare for up to 20 children and 3 employees at 21 Young, and other land use changes from a January 28 public hearing.

chips.text: Property owners in Aspen Ridge, 193023 West, and 7702704 Central Avenue.
Administration recommended denying the daycare, but Council approved an altered motion.
